Team — attaching the raw decomposition (redwood_usage_breakdown_May2027.csv) and a short ROI recap. Highlights:

- Root cause: 68% of the incremental tokens came from the "product-recs" route after the new multi-shot candidate scoring landed (average context length jumped from 1.1k -> 3.8k).
- Secondary: short-lived spike in interactive debug sessions (internal sandbox users) accounted for 12% — recommend a quota for non-prod traffic.
- Token mix: 72% inference (generation), 28% embeddings/rerank.

I'll include an itemized per-route avg latency and cost-per-1k-tokens in the deck. Suggestions:
1) Short-term smoothing: enable response-length caps on the product-recs route + prefix caching (expected ~35% reduction).
2) 12-month commit + 20% headroom: improves unit economics by ~18% on our model profile.
3) Hybrid: Reserved baseline for production traffic + burst credits for experiments — best for teams with seasonality.

Attachments: redwood_usage_breakdown_May2027.csv; roi-recap-everlane-q1-q2-2027.xlsx

Marissa Cole

Subject: RE: Renewal check + quick ask on May spike — proposal attached

Asha / Ranjit — attaching a concise proposal (term_scenarios_pricing_v2.pdf) with hard monthly deltas and an ROI summary. Executive bullets below:

- Baseline (month-to-month): projected average monthly spend based on current run-rate: $72,400/mo.
- Short-term smoothing (3-month policy + response caps): estimated $47k–$55k/mo (35–45% reduction depending on adoption of caps).
- 12-month commit + 20% headroom: effective average $59,400/mo (18% unit discount vs baseline) and 1.5% commit credit applied in months 1–3 to offset onboarding.
- 18-month commit (your ask): $53,800/mo effective with an additional adoption credit that phases out after month 6 — modeled as a $40k one-time credit applied against months 1–3. Net present value improves ~9% vs 12m commit.
- Hybrid reserved + burst: baseline reserved for prod (60% of steady-state) + burst credits for experiments. Estimated $61k–$65k/mo depending on burst consumption.

Recommendation: If Everlane expects continued rollout across squads, the 18-month with adoption credit gives predictable economics and covers ramp risk. If you want flexibility, the hybrid route preserves headroom for experiments.

Next steps:
1) If this looks directionally right, I can generate a line-item quote for procurement (DocuSign-ready).
2) Schedule a 30-min walkthrough for Monday to talk adoption credits and SLAs.

Attachments: term_scenarios_pricing_v2.pdf; roi-recap-everlane-q1-q2-2027.xlsx

—Karthik
